item.title: Fri Oct 30: A vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid, Floquet physics from dark excitons, and stripes before superconductivity in moiré tungsten diselenide
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid — Ryan L. Lee et al.
    STM imaging of a charged vortex-antivortex lattice in a bilayer graphene exciton condensate provides direct, striking evidence of phase coherence and fractionally charged vortices in an exciton superfluid.
  2. Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum — Xing Zhu et al.
    Time- and angle-resolved photoemission on WSe2/MoS2 heterostructures shows that dense incoherent dark interlayer excitons can mimic Floquet band hybridization for nearly a nanosecond, opening a new non-equilibrium route to engineer electronic structure with excitons.
  3. Charge Filling-Dependent Valley Polarization and its Dynamics Driven by Correlated Interlayer Exciton States in WSe2/WS2 Heterobilayer — Zhiwei Li et al.
    Direct demonstration that correlated interlayer exciton states at integer moiré filling in WSe2/WS2 control valley relaxation dynamics, linking valleytronics to Mott physics in a heterobilayer central to the group's interests.
  4. Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator — Yichi Zhang et al.
    Transport evidence for stripe (electronic liquid crystal) phases and a stripe-to-superconductor quantum phase transition upon doping a moiré Mott insulator in twisted bilayer WSe2, a rare controllable platform for cuprate-like intertwined orders.
  5. Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| \geq 1 in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene — Qiu Yang et al.
    Observation of coexisting unconventional superconductivity and high Chern number (|C|>=1) insulators in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene reveals a rich interplay of topology and pairing in a moiré flat-band system.

Briefs

  1. Chiral p-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moiré Chern Band — Yunze Ouyang et al.
    Exact diagonalization finds chiral p-wave superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator and topological charge density wave in a moiré Chern band of twisted MoTe2, directly relevant to current fractional Chern insulator physics.
  2. The Flexoelectric Twist: Persistence of Heavy Fermion Picture in Small-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene — Qirong Yao et al.
    STM on small-angle twisted bilayer graphene shows lattice reconstruction and flexoelectric coupling sustain a heavy-fermion/Kondo-lattice picture even away from the magic angle.
  3. Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands — Magnus Husted et al.
    Atomistic tight-binding calculations predict moiré-tunable chiral (Born-Kuhn) plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands, a new optical handle on twist-angle physics.
  4. Few-Electron Partitioning in the Fractional Quantum Hall Regime — T. Jonckheere et al.
    A solvable theory of few-electron partitioning at a fractional quantum Hall point contact predicts antibunching and higher-order correlations directly testable in recent Levitons experiments.
  5. HERA: Assessing an Autonomous Agent for Quantum Device Measurement — Zachary W. Gomez et al.
    An autonomous LLM-based agent (HERA) matches expert conclusions in blinded cryogenic transport measurements on graphene devices, a notable proof-of-concept for AI-driven experimental quantum materials research.

item.title: Tue Oct 27: Moiré excitons read by graphene, chiral pairing next to a Wigner crystal, and compressing quantum Hall images
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moiré excitons — Katsunori Wakabayashi
    Proposes graphene near-field energy transfer as a momentum-resolved spectroscopy for dark/chiral moiré excitons in WSe2/MoSe2, directly extending the toolkit for probing optically dark states central to your research.
  2. Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene — Ke Wang
    Shows how electronic correlations driving Wigner crystallization in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene can also seed chiral f-wave superconductivity nearby, linking two of your core interests (Wigner crystals and correlated 2D electronic phases).
  3. Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter — Chen Wu et al.
    Introduces an information-theoretic 'entropy imaging' technique applied to microwave impedance microscopy of graphene that quantitatively tracks spatial complexity across integer and fractional quantum Hall transitions, including isolated fractional puddles and a moiré heterobilayer comparison.
  4. Nanoscale mapping of native defects in Td-MoTe2 and their impact on graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures — Wojciech Ry\'s et al.
    STM/STS mapping of native Te-vacancy defects in Td-MoTe2 and their (weak) impact on graphene/MoTe2 van der Waals heterostructures speaks directly to interface characterization relevant to your heterostructure optics work.
  5. Second-Harmonic Bulk Response of Fractional Quantum Hall Fluids — J. Luke Pimlott et al.
    Develops a bulk composite-boson theory for second-harmonic Hall response of fractional quantum Hall fluids, giving a new finite-frequency nonlinear probe of FQH physics beyond edge-mode theories.

Briefs

  1. Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between PT-Partner States in 2H-bilayer MoS2 — Fred Sun et al.
    Analyzes helicity-selective chiral-phonon coupling to PT-degenerate electronic doublets in bilayer MoS2, offering a new symmetry-based readout scheme for TMD valley/pseudospin states.
  2. Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network — D. B. Karki et al.
    Demonstrates a tunable, relocatable emergent Z3 parafermion in a triangular triple-quantum-dot circuit, a concrete non-Abelian-anyon platform complementary to quantum Hall anyon physics.
  3. Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi — Yuto Fukushima et al.
    Spin-ARPES directly resolves a sizable, magnetism-linked Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi, resolving a long-standing discrepancy relevant to quantized anomalous Hall physics in AFM-TIs.
  4. Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry — Runxin Li et al.
    Atomic-scale Josephson interferometry on monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3 reveals an intra-unit-cell nodal pattern that fingerprints nodeless d-wave pairing, a striking new phase-sensitive probe technique for unconventional superconductors.
  5. Zeptojoule Microwave Calorimetry with Nanosecond Recovery in Graphene — Seunghan Lee et al.
    Careful calibration of a graphene Josephson-junction microwave calorimeter pinpoints the microscopic origin (enhanced heat capacity and electron-phonon coupling) of the gap between ideal and achieved zeptojoule-scale sensitivity in graphene-based quantum sensors.

item.title: Mon Oct 26: Quantum-capacitance optics, an M-point flat band, and composite fermions that decay into electrons
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures — Xiangzhi Hong et al.
    Shows quantum capacitance, not just geometric gating, governs interlayer exciton Stark shifts in vdW heterostructures, directly relevant to optical probing of electrostatics in 2D systems.
  2. Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the \barM point in 2.4\deg twisted bilayer graphene — Giovanna Feraco et al.
    First nano-ARPES observation of a flat band away from the K point in twisted bilayer graphene, revealing new momentum-space structure relevant to moire correlated physics.
  3. Spontaneous Decay of High Energy Composite Fermions — Mytraya Gattu et al.
    Jain and collaborators show high-energy composite fermions in the fractional quantum Hall fluid spontaneously decay into quasiparticles, quasiholes and electrons, a conceptually important result for FQH physics.
  4. Magnons and excitons from Bethe-Salpeter equation and its application to graphene-based magnets — Simran Chourasia et al.
    Develops a unified Bethe-Salpeter framework capturing both excitons and gapless magnons in 2D magnetic materials like graphene-based magnets, bridging exciton and spin-wave physics central to the listener's optical spectroscopy interests.
  5. Optical signatures of Rashba–Dresselhaus coupling across Franz–Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors — Bahruz Suleymanli et al.
    Predicts distinct optical (Franz-Keldysh/Landau) signatures that disentangle Rashba vs Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling in 2D semiconductors, directly relevant to optical probes of 2D material band structure.

Briefs

  1. Heat current and noise in a point-like junction between normal metal and fractional quantum hall edge state with \nu = 1/3 — Redouane Zamoum et al.
    Computes heat noise and a modified Wiedemann-Franz law at a nu=1/3 fractional quantum Hall point contact, extending edge-state transport theory relevant to the listener's quantum Hall interests.
  2. Multifractal Magnons Around Localized Defects — Adarsh Hullahalli et al.
    Demonstrates that localized defects and skyrmions can induce multifractal magnon wavefunctions in clean 2D magnets, observable via uniform ac fields.
  3. Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices — Hongyu Li et al.
    Reveals a heterogeneous, spatially-varying superconducting gap emerging from a charge-stripe CDW in kagome superconductors, a surprising cooperative CDW-superconductivity phenomenon outside the core focus but broadly significant.
  4. Magnonic time crystal with lasing coherence — Jiantao Song et al.
    Realizes a room-temperature magnonic discrete time crystal with laser-like coherence and narrow linewidth, a surprising nonequilibrium phase of matter result worth broad awareness.
  5. Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering — Chunjing Jia et al.
    Proposes an X-ray RIXS analogue of the DLCZ protocol to herald entanglement between distant regions of a solid via photon interference, a novel quantum-optics-meets-quantum-materials technique.

item.title: Fri Oct 23: Bosonic edges in twisted TMDs, reversed-drift anyons, and stripes versus superconductivity
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift — Zhenyu Xiao et al.
    Shows that Laughlin quasiholes in a modulated magnetic field acquire their own Chern bands with opposite-sign topology and anomalous (reversed) drift, directly relevant to anyon/fractional quantum Hall physics in Chern-insulator-like 2D systems.
  2. Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator — Andreas Feuerpfeil et al.
    Numerically confirms a predicted bosonic edge phase in double quantum spin Hall insulators and explicitly connects it to twisted WSe2/MoTe2 homobilayers, directly bearing on moire TMD physics.
  3. Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices — Muhammad Akram et al.
    Maps out charge-density-wave phases and symmetry-protected bound states in lattice-mismatched moire superlattices built from coupled SSH chains, offering a tractable model for moire electronic reconstruction.
  4. Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model — Ao Chen et al.
    State-of-the-art neural-network variational simulations reveal extreme near-degeneracy between stripe and d-wave superconducting states in the doped Hubbard model, reshaping the leading theoretical narrative for cuprates.
  5. Discrete time liquids — Zuo Wang et al.
    Identifies a genuinely new non-equilibrium phase, 'discrete time liquids' with finite temporal coherence from time-solitons, extending the time-crystal paradigm to noisy cavity-coupled spin systems.

Briefs

  1. \pi-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model — Zhaochen Liu et al.
    Compares flux-tuned triangular-lattice Hubbard models to show how ring-exchange sign controls chiral spin liquid formation, relevant background theory for moire triangular-lattice TMD systems.
  2. Reentrant d=2+1 Superfluidity at High Temperature — Subham Dutta Chowdhury et al.
    Constructs a UV-complete 2+1D model with a BKT-ordered phase persisting to arbitrarily high temperature, a surprising result in quantum statistical mechanics.
  3. Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector — Pawe{\l} Mrowi\'nski et al.
    Demonstrates a monolithic telecom-band InAs/InP quantum dot single-photon source with decent two-photon interference visibility without cavity Purcell enhancement, relevant to quantum photonics hardware.
  4. Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology — Yu Zhang
    Proposes that a chiral cavity vacuum can locally generate and probe non-Abelian topological masses in the Kitaev model, linking cavity QED to topological matter engineering.
  5. Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo — Yin-Kai Yu et al.
    Introduces a sign-problem-free auxiliary-field QMC scheme for frustrated bosonic lattice models, a notable numerical methods advance for strongly correlated bosons.

  1. The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond — Maciej R. Molas
    A comprehensive review mapping the full hierarchy of excitonic complexes (trions, biexcitons, Rydberg states, dark excitons, hexcitons, oxcitons) in hBN-encapsulated TMD monolayers, directly serving as a field reference for the listener's core research area.
  2. Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model — Jiahao Yang et al.
    Studies electron fractionalization into spinons and chargons in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model on a triangular lattice, directly relevant to correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré TMD systems and predicting ARPES/STM signatures.
  3. Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets — Lingxian Kong et al.
    Predicts a dynamical tunneling blockade from valley-pseudospin precession in layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, a novel nonequilibrium phenomenon in double-layer quantum Hall/moiré systems tied closely to valley physics.
  4. Interplay of disorder and phonons in two-dimensional transport — Aryaman Babbar et al.
    A detailed Boltzmann-transport analysis of disorder and phonon scattering in bilayer MoSe2 that reinterprets resistivity-minimum phenomenology relevant to correlated-state detection in TMD monolayers.
  5. Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa2Cu3O6+x — K. Kaj et al.
    Resolves a long-standing ambiguity in THz pump-probe experiments on YBCO, confirming genuine light-induced high-temperature superconducting optical signatures — a landmark result in nonequilibrium quantum materials outside the core profile.

Briefs

  1. Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructures — Haozhe Yang et al.
    Demonstrates electric-field control of spin texture and spin-charge interconversion in a HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, relevant to 2D material spin-orbit engineering.
  2. Interaction-Induced Bloch Geometry and Transverse Thermoelectric Transport — Heng-Yu Di et al.
    Derives how electron-electron interactions reconstruct Berry curvature and quantum metric in a triangular-lattice Hubbard model, with direct relevance to correlated moiré flat-band thermoelectric transport.
  3. Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors — Jia-Long Zhang et al.
    Develops a quantum-geometric theory of optical anomalous Hall response in time-reversal-breaking superconductors, offering a new optical probe concept analogous to techniques used in 2D exciton spectroscopy.
  4. High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence — Chia-Hsien Huang et al.
    Presents an optimal-control framework achieving near-speed-limit, high-fidelity CZ gates for transmon qubits with built-in noise robustness, a significant advance for scalable superconducting quantum computing outside the core profile.
  5. Ubiquitous topological materials protected by hidden partial symmetries — Lumen Eek et al.
    Introduces 'partial latent symmetries' that can protect approximately quantized topological edge states even without full system-wide symmetry, broadening the conceptual toolkit for topological phases relevant to flat-band/Chern physics.

item.title: Wed Oct 21: Darkening excitons, exciton density limits, cooperative LEDs, and an anticrystal in graphene
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Magnetic-Field-Induced Darkening of Bright Excitons in a MoWSe2 Monolayer Alloy — Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko et al.
    Demonstrates a new magneto-optical control mechanism—field-induced darkening of bright excitons via bright-dark mixing in an alloyed TMD monolayer—directly relevant to valley/exciton spectroscopy in 2D materials.
  2. Density Saturation and Autocorrelation Characteristics of Interlayer Exciton Ensembles in MoSe2/WSe2 Heterostructures — Mirco Troue et al.
    Maps the density-temperature phase diagram of interlayer excitons in MoSe2/WSe2 heterostructures and finds saturation consistent with a Mott transition, core to exciton physics in vdW heterostructures.
  3. Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes — Andr\'es M. Mier Valdivia et al.
    Reports steady-state superradiant/cooperative emission from electrically injected interlayer excitons in a 2D TMD LED, a striking collective quantum optics phenomenon in exactly the author's experimental platform.
  4. Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene — Daniele Guerci et al.
    Proposes hole crystallization (an 'anticrystal') to explain anomalous quantum oscillations near the superconducting phase of rhombohedral graphene, tying correlated electronic states to Fermi-surface physics in a flagship moiré-adjacent 2D system.
  5. Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin — Bingxuan Jiang et al.
    Introduces a new quantum-geometric framework for the layer pseudospin in twisted MoTe2 bilayers, predicting moiré-periodic optical responses directly relevant to moiré TMD spectroscopy.

Briefs

  1. Adiabatic confinement and number-theoretic spectra of massless Dirac fermions in twisted trilayer graphene — Kunihiro Yananose et al.
    Finds a novel relativistic confinement mechanism for massless Dirac fermions in twisted trilayer graphene domains, linking moiré engineering to number-theoretic spectral structure.
  2. Stacking-Induced Tuning of a Flat-Band Surface State in NbIrTe4 — Jiabin Yu et al.
    STM/ARPES study shows a flat-band surface state in the layered TMDC NbIrTe4 is tunable by local stacking order, relevant to stacking-controlled 2D electronic structure.
  3. Neural Network Fractional Quantum Hall States with Learnable Orbital Pair Matrix Factors: Balancing Physical Priors and Flexibility — Yubing Qian et al.
    Improves neural-network variational wavefunctions for fractional quantum Hall states with Landau-level mixing, a methodological advance relevant to QH physics interests.
  4. Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points — Reja H. Wilke et al.
    Identifies spectroscopic (RIXS/neutron) fingerprints of elusive hidden-order and hidden quantum-critical phases in doped spin chains, a surprising result broadening beyond the core 2D-optics focus.
  5. Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas — Hai-Ying Cui et al.
    Exact Bethe-ansatz solution predicts a clean spectroscopic signature of the long-sought Luther-Emery liquid in 1D attractive Fermi gases, a notable result in quantum liquids outside the core profile.

item.title: Tue Oct 20: High-temperature kagome flat bands, proximity transient absorption, and superconductivity's topological floor
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics — Hyungkun Bong et al.
    First realization of an ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattice with nano-ARPES-resolved flat bands at ~220x higher density than moire systems, opening a new high-density flat-band platform directly relevant to 2D material band engineering.
  2. Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A2T3X4 — Soomin Oh et al.
    Companion theory paper predicting fractional Chern insulators, composite Fermi liquids and fractional quantum spin Hall phases at greatly enhanced temperatures in the new vdW kagome family, a major step for FCI physics beyond moire systems.
  3. Proximity Transient Absorption in van der Waals Heterostructures — Neema Rafizadeh et al.
    Demonstrates a new 'proximity transient absorption' modality where a WS2 exciton optically reports on photoexcited carrier dynamics in a neighboring graphene layer through an hBN spacer, directly relevant to optical probes of vdW heterostructures.
  4. Strain-induced disorder from Schottky gates on high mobility 2DEGs — Sambit Mohapatra et al.
    Identifies strain from granular Schottky gate films as the microscopic origin of mobility degradation in high-mobility 2DEGs, a key practical issue for gated fractional quantum Hall experiments.
  5. Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness — Zhi-Wei Wang et al.
    Derives an exact topological lower bound on superfluid stiffness for vortexable Chern flat bands, sharpening the theoretical foundation for ideal fractional Chern insulators and flat-band superconductivity.

Briefs

  1. Topological Quantum Gates on FCIs with Bounded Quantum Geometry — Hisham Sati et al.
    Shows that bounded quantum geometry in Chern-|C|>1 FCIs can enable non-Clifford topological gates (T-gate, CCZ), a novel link between quantum geometry and fault-tolerant quantum computation.
  2. Unconventional spin momentum locking and topological domains in twisted slabs of topological insulator Bi2Te3 — Thomas Naimer et al.
    First-principles study of twisted Bi2Te3 slabs reveals moire-scale topological domains and unconventional radial spin textures, extending twistronics concepts to 3D topological insulators.
  3. Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite — Arthur C. Campello et al.
    High-resolution neutron scattering plus DMRG on herbertsmithite reveals two nearly degenerate, coexisting quantum spin liquid states, resolving a long-standing puzzle in frustrated magnetism.
  4. The Anyon Atlas — Jonah Berean-Dutcher et al.
    A systematic classification of anyon theories up to 22-26 types uncovers topological orders that cannot be built from any known Chern-Simons theory, a surprising structural result for anyonic/quantum Hall physics.
  5. Kohler's Rule Holds in the Strange Metallic Hubbard Model — Rebekah M. Jin et al.
    Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo on the strange-metal Hubbard model finds Kohler's rule unexpectedly holds despite T-linear resistivity and absent quasiparticles, challenging common lore about anomalous magnetotransport.

item.title: Mon Oct 19: Anyons bound to excitons, attraction from repulsion in Chern bands, and a neural net for the free anyon gas
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Anyon bound states in MoTe2 Fractional Chern Insulators — Tianhong Lu et al.
    Direct real-space characterization of anyon-exciton bound states in a twisted MoTe2 FCI connects exciton optics to fractional quantum Hall physics, squarely at the intersection of this listener's moire and optics interests.
  2. Fractional Chern insulators and composite Fermi liquids vs. charge order in twisted MoTe2 — Enrique Aguilar-M\'endez et al.
    A comprehensive exact-diagonalization phase diagram of FCIs, composite Fermi liquids, and charge order in twisted MoTe2 directly addresses the moire/fractional Chern insulator physics central to the listener's secondary focus.
  3. Attraction from repulsion in an interacting Chern band: chiral superconductivity, generalized Hall crystals, and competing fractional Chern insulators — Fabian Pichler et al.
    Tensor-network study revealing how fluctuation-induced attraction connects FCIs to chiral superconductivity and Hall crystals in Chern bands offers deep insight into the competing orders seen in recent moire experiments.
  4. From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots — Klaus D. J\"ons et al.
    A perspective on the evolution of semiconductor quantum dots as single/entangled photon sources is highly relevant to the listener's quantum photonics group context and future device directions.
  5. Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions — Andres Perez Fadon et al.
    Novel neural-network wavefunction technique pushes anyon gas simulations to unprecedented particle numbers, giving fresh numerical access to fractional statistics physics underlying FCI states.

Briefs

  1. Valley-Selective Transport through Structural Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene Quarter Metals — Vo Tien Phong et al.
    Distinguishes structural vs. intrinsic valley domain walls in rhombohedral graphene quarter metals via magnetotransport, relevant to moire/valley physics.
  2. Quantum-interference correction to conductivity in disordered electronic bands with non-uniform quantum geometry — Yip Chun Wong et al.
    Shows how nonuniform quantum geometry in rhombohedral graphene can flip weak localization to antilocalization, linking quantum geometry (a core moire concept) to transport.
  3. Transport Signatures of a Kinetically Self-Trapped Nagaoka Polaron — Yusong Xiao et al.
    Computes transport signatures of a self-trapped Nagaoka polaron, offering a transport analog to the polaron physics the listener studies optically.
  4. Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin — Enbo Zhang et al.
    Demonstrates chirality-resolved magnon imaging using NV centers, a surprising and broadly important quantum sensing technique outside the core focus.
  5. Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor — Ruizhe Shen et al.
    First quantum-processor realization of a Landau-forbidden deconfined quantum critical transition, a genuinely notable result worth a quick mention for broader context.

item.title: Thu Oct 15: Anyons caught at trion traps, forcing weak excitons to absorb, and squeezing moiré potentials with pressure
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Anyons at impurities: Fractional charge measurement and "wrong sign" binding — Haydn S. Adlong et al.
    Direct theoretical follow-up on twisted MoTe2 anyon-trion binding experiments from Imamoglu's own group, revealing surprising 'wrong-sign' binding and probing anyon internal structure via optically trapped excitons/trions.
  2. Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling — Saroj Poudyal et al.
    Demonstrates Purcell engineering of cavity critical coupling to boost weak interlayer exciton absorption by an order of magnitude, a powerful new technique for probing dipolar excitons in TMD bilayers.
  3. Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices — Wenbing Li et al.
    Combines diamond anvil pressure cells with dual-gated twisted WSe2/WS2 optical spectroscopy to continuously tune the moiré potential landscape and exciton-charge interactions, a novel knob for moiré exciton physics.
  4. Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe2/CrI3 heterostructures — Natalie Kuhn et al.
    Helicity-resolved spectroscopy of WSe2/CrI3 heterostructures shows that trion valley physics is sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic order of the adjacent 2D magnet, not just the interfacial layer, refining the magnetic proximity picture central to TMD valleytronics.
  5. Nanoscale Mapping of Strain-engineered Excitons in Monolayer WSe2 — Anna S. Roche et al.
    Cryogenic s-SNOM nanoscale mapping directly correlates strain and exciton energy shifts in monolayer WSe2, resolving the long-standing ambiguity about the origin of strain-induced single-photon emitters.

  1. Metallic electron crystals in rhombohedral graphene as a bridge to twisted WSe2 — Wentai Deng et al.

    First-principles neural-network variational wavefunctions identify Ising-type non-Abelian anyons at nu=3/2 with full Landau-level mixing, a significant advance for fractional quantum Hall anyon physics.
  3. Nodal nematic superconductivity in moiré graphene — Shuwen Sun et al.
    Tunneling and transport evidence for an intrinsic nodal nematic superconducting state in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene that spontaneously breaks moiré lattice rotational symmetry.
  4. Chern insulator optics — Jason G. Kattan et al.
    Develops a field theory for the unusual long-wavelength optical activity and giant Faraday/Kerr rotations of Chern insulators like MnBi2Te4, connecting topology to directly measurable optics.

item.title: Mon Oct 12: Dark excitons in gallium nitride, Rydberg exciton orbital transfer, and a Cooper instability in a Wigner crystal
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Real-Time Relaxation Dynamics of Dark Excitons in Mirror-Symmetric Monolayers — Rishabh Saraswat et al.
    Derives exact exciton-phonon selection rules from mirror parity in D3h monolayers and solves real-time Boltzmann dynamics for dark exciton relaxation, directly bearing on dark-exciton physics central to your work.
  2. Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons — Mengli Wang et al.
    Tests how far a Rytova-Keldysh effective Hamiltonian for Rydberg excitons can be transferred to unmeasured states, finding material-specific deviations in MoSe2 vs WS2 that probe dielectric screening beyond the standard model.
  3. Theory of exciton-exciton interactions in crystalline systems — L. Maisel Licer\'an et al.
    Develops a general microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions valid for topological/moiré bands, showing biexciton spectra are strongly modified by quantum geometry—directly relevant to correlated excitonic phases in moiré TMDs.
  4. Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe2/WSe2 with a Monolayer hBN Spacer — Johannes Figueiredo et al.
    Shows a monolayer hBN spacer suppresses atomic reconstruction in twisted MoSe2/WSe2, a practical knob for achieving the lateral homogeneity needed for collective moiré-exciton experiments.
  5. Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal — Wangqian Miao et al.
    Finds that collective modes of a magnetic Wigner crystal in rhombohedral graphene can mediate chiral p-wave pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry, connecting Wigner-crystal physics to emergent superconductivity—a hot topic in correlated 2D electronic states.

Briefs

  1. Vacuum-field-mediated Landau-level reconstruction in a cavity-coupled two-dimensional electron gas — Zi-Heng Zhu et al.
    Shows a structured cavity vacuum field can reconstruct integer quantum Hall Landau levels via a finite-momentum ladder while preserving Chern numbers, a clean cavity-QED twist on 2D quantum Hall physics.
  2. Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states — Mytraya Gattu et al.
    Parton-theory calculations identify the ν=1/2 state in wide quantum wells as an especially promising candidate for free (unbound) non-Abelian quasiparticles in even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states.
  3. An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor — Chan Bin Bark et al.
    First digital-quantum-processor realization of doublon-holon scattering in the Fermi-Hubbard model, matching Bethe-ansatz predictions and directly probing entanglement generation in quasiparticle collisions.
  4. Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search — Qiang Gao
    An AI-assisted (Claude-driven) semidefinite-programming search dramatically tightens the rigorous lower bound on the Laughlin spectral gap, a notable example of AI-accelerated proof techniques in quantum Hall theory.
  5. Graphene double quantum dot as a solid-state two-level system in the THz range — Alexis Wietzke et al.
    Demonstrates an hBN-encapsulated graphene double quantum dot acting as a solid-state two-level system with a THz transition frequency, a new 2D-material platform for THz quantum technology.

item.title: Wed Oct 7: Quantum geometry by QTM, composite fermions in rhombohedral graphene, and Raman interference in WSe2
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Quantum twisting microscopy as a momentum-resolved probe of quantum geometry and sublattice symmetries — Lucas V. Pupim et al.
    Proposes using the quantum twisting microscope with sublattice-polarized tips to directly measure quantum geometry and symmetry signatures in moiré graphene, a direct extension of the QTM technique central to this research area.
  2. Theory of resonance Raman profiles in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers: Interference effects due to inter-valley phonon scattering — Daniel Groll et al.
    A microscopic theory of resonance Raman profiles in WSe2 explains destructive interference from inter-valley K-Q phonon scattering, directly relevant to exciton-phonon spectroscopy in TMD monolayers.
  3. Composite Fermion Theory of Fractional Chern Insulators in Rhombohedral Graphene — Peize Ding et al.
    Develops a composite fermion theory explaining how moiré potential and Coulomb interactions stabilize the fractional Chern insulator states recently observed in rhombohedral graphene, bridging FCI and quantum Hall physics.
  4. Direct synthesis of moiré graphene with twist-tuned hybridization — Seunghyun Park et al.
    Demonstrates a reconfigurable MEMS-based platform for in-situ, continuously tunable twisted graphene with Raman-resolved phonon folding, offering a new tool for moiré material fabrication and characterization.
  5. Interfacial Charge Transfer and Morphology Govern Magnetism in Ultrathin VOx/MoSe2 Heterostructures — Yasinthara Wadumesthri et al.
    Shows interfacial charge transfer from VOx to monolayer MoSe2 enhances magnetism while simultaneously boosting trion weight in photoluminescence, directly linking optical spectroscopy to induced magnetism in a vdW heterostructure.

  1. Theory of Magic Angles in Twisted Bilayer Graphene: from Non-Abelian Gauge Fields to Flat Bands — Leonardo A. Navarro-Labastida et al.

  2. Ultra-small-angle graphene twistronics with monolayer spacers: From interlayer hybridisation and moiré effects to high-temperature magnetotransport oscillations — Benjamin Fuller et al.
    Predicts miniband structure, Lifshitz transitions, and high-temperature Brown-Zak-like magnetoresistance oscillations in ultra-small-angle twisted graphene with a monolayer hBN spacer.
  3. Sparse qubit operation in a 6\times6 quantum dot array — Alexader S. Ivlev et al.
    Demonstrates a scalable 6x6 semiconductor quantum dot array with sparse shuttling-based qubit operation, a notable step for 2D-scalable quantum computing architectures.
  4. Chiral Parafermions in Floquet \mathbbZN Topological Order — Melissa Will et al.

item.title: Tue Oct 6: Open orbits toward fractional Chern insulators, paired composite fermions, and terahertz imaging of shift currents
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Beyond the Flat-Band Paradigm: Open Orbits as a Route to Correlated States in Dispersive Moiré Minibands — Zihao Wang et al.
    Proposes and observes incipient fractional Chern insulator-like transport signatures in dispersive (non-flat-band) moiré minibands of graphene/hBN, directly challenging the flat-band paradigm central to your moiré interests.
  2. Escaping the Composite Fermi Sea: An Incompressible State at Half Filling in Graphene's Lowest Landau Level — Domagoj Perkovic et al.
    Exact diagonalization and DMRG study identifying a strongly-paired composite-fermion mechanism for the puzzling incompressible even-denominator states seen at half filling in graphene's lowest Landau level.
  3. Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene — Bogdan Borodin et al.
    Cryogenic polarization-resolved terahertz nanoscopy cleanly isolates the bulk photovoltaic effect in bilayer graphene, revealing quantum-geometric signatures like trigonal warping via a nanoscale optical probe.
  4. Exchange-controlled quantum beats and entanglement in an exciton–bimodal-cavity system — Cesar E. P. Villegas et al.
    Theoretical framework for tunable exciton-exciton exchange and long-lived entanglement generation in an exciton-bimodal-cavity system, parameterized with first-principles exciton parameters, directly relevant to cavity-coupled exciton physics.
  5. Floquet dressing of bulk metallic bands in 2H-NbSe2 — Cong Li et al.
    First clear demonstration of Floquet dressing in the itinerant bulk bands of a multiband metal (2H-NbSe2) via time-resolved ARPES, extending coherent optical control beyond surface/2D Dirac systems where it was thought unfeasible.

Briefs

  1. Density Functional Theory for 2D Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides with Extended Hubbard Parameters — Xue Li et al.
    Introduces an efficient DFT+Hubbard-U/V framework that quantitatively reproduces spin-orbit splittings and band gaps across MoS2/MoSe2/WS2/WSe2, useful for high-throughput TMD modeling.
  2. Intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in graphene stacks — Guillermo Parra-Martinez et al.
    Shows intrinsic spin-orbit coupling, usually neglected in graphene, has important consequences for Fermi surfaces and magnetization in rhombohedral multilayer graphene stacks relevant to moiré/graphene physics.
  3. Distilling universal machine-learning potentials for moiré lattices across one million atoms — Thomas Huang et al.
    A machine-learned interatomic potential enabling million-atom simulations of moiré reconstruction, revealing hierarchical polarization textures at moiré-of-moiré domain walls in twisted TMD trilayers.
  4. Peeling off Abelian Anyons and Proliferation Transitions — Meng Cheng et al.
    A general field-theoretic framework for 'peeling off' Abelian anyons from 2+1D TQFTs to systematically construct and classify anyon-condensation phase transitions, of broad relevance to topological order.
  5. Does a pole in the self-energy imply a violation of the Luttinger theorem? — Artem Abanov et al.
    A surprising theoretical result showing that a pole in the self-energy does not necessarily violate the Luttinger theorem, clarifying a widely assumed breakdown condition in strongly correlated Fermi liquids.

item.title: Mon Oct 5: Moiré metamagnetism, field-tuned Wigner crystals, and cleaning up anyon noise
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Correlated Metals, Metamagnetism, and Orbital Nematic Order in moiré Materials with Neural Quantum States — Wei Zhang et al.
    Imamoglu-group neural-quantum-state study reveals correlated metal, metamagnetic, and orbital nematic phases in moiré triangular lattices, directly extending the group's own theoretical interests in correlated 2D electronic states.
  2. Magnetic-field response of generalized Wigner crystals in twisted MoTe2 — F. K. Wolff et al.
    Magnetotransport reveals how a perpendicular field selectively stabilizes or suppresses generalized Wigner crystal states in twisted MoTe2, a direct probe of correlated moiré charge order central to the profile.
  3. Electrostatic Doping of Moiré Superlattices Controls the Optical Fingerprint of a WSe2 /Twisted Bilayer Graphene heterostructure — Houssem Eddine Hannachi et al.
    Theory shows that electrostatic doping of a WSe2/twisted bilayer graphene heterostructure produces satellite exciton resonances via Rydberg-state hybridization, a concrete optical-probe proposal for moiré-coupled TMD excitons.
  4. Quantum materials QED with van der Waals crystals — Suheng Xu et al.
    Demonstrates ultrastrong mid-IR coupling between graphene Landau-level transitions and hBN phonons in van der Waals multilayer cavities, establishing a new materials-QED platform relevant to cavity-coupled 2D systems.
  5. Extracting the anyon charge from shot noise in complex fractional quantum Hall edges — Jinhong Park et al.
    Develops a framework to cleanly extract anyon charge from shot noise in multichannel fractional quantum Hall edges despite equilibration heating, advancing a key experimental tool for anyonic/edge-state physics.

Briefs

  1. Chiral Vacuum Engineering of Quantum Hall Matter — Kiran M. Kulkarni et al.
    Predicts that cavity chirality produces handedness-dependent corrections to Hall resistivity and a squeezed vacuum ground state in cavity-coupled 2D electron gases, linking quantum Hall physics to cavity QED.
  2. Melting phase diagram of the two-dimensional electron solid in a perpendicular magnetic field — M. Yu. Melnikov et al.
    Measures the thermal melting phase diagram of the 2D Wigner electron crystal in a magnetic field, finding an unexpected plateau attributed to crystallite resonance modes.
  3. Layer-Asymmetry-Induced Topological Superconductivity in High-Tc Bilayer Nickelates — Zhongyi Zhang et al.
    Proposes that layer-asymmetric bilayer nickelate thin films can realize time-reversal-invariant topological superconductivity with Majorana edge modes, a notable extension of the high-Tc nickelate story.
  4. Ab initio Green's function theory of superfluid neutron matter — F. Marino et al.
    First ab initio Gorkov Green's-function calculation of pairing gaps and spectral signatures of superfluidity across the full density range of neutron star matter, a significant nuclear-astrophysics result.
  5. Fluctuation-induced magnetoresistance in graphene Hall bars at charge neutrality — Anna Grigoreva et al.
    Derives analytic magnetoresistance formulas for hydrodynamic electron flow in graphene at charge neutrality, showing strong positive MR sensitive to Hall-bar geometry.

item.title: Thu Oct 1: Electrically Switchable Topological Polaritons, a New Probe for Twisted Molybdenum Disulfide, and Quantum Hall Quantization Hiding in Dissipation
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Topological Fermi-polaron Polaritons with Electrically Invertible Topology — Xin Xie et al.
    Demonstrates electrically invertible topological Fermi-polaron polaritons in a gate-tunable monolayer TMD photonic crystal, directly combining exciton-polariton physics, many-body interactions, and band topology central to the listener's work.
  2. Qantum Well Resonant Tunneling Diode Probe of Correlated States in Twisted Bilayer MoS2 — Chengjie Zhou et al.
    A new quantum-well resonant tunneling diode probe reveals integer and generalized-Wigner-crystal correlated insulating states in twisted bilayer MoS2, a prime example of electronic detection of correlated moire states.
  3. Optical observation of interlayer spin correlation — Akiyoshi Park et al.
    First direct optical probe of interlayer spin correlations in a vdW antiferromagnet via two-magnon Raman scattering, with an exciton-resonance-enhanced variant extendable to twisted bilayers—squarely in the optical-detection-of-correlated-states niche.
  4. Atomic-Scale Imaging of Lattice Relaxation and Topological Flat Bands in Helical Trilayer Graphene — Shudan Jiang et al.
    Combined SNOM and STM imaging of helical trilayer graphene uncovers lattice relaxation, topological flat bands, and a larger-than-predicted magic angle, directly relevant to moire materials and flat-band physics.
  5. Quantization through Dissipation and the Optical Quantum Hall Effect — Zhenisbek Tagay et al.
    Reveals a new optical/dissipative route to understanding integer quantum Hall quantization via terahertz Faraday rotation, connecting finite-frequency optics to topological transport—bridging the listener's optics and quantum Hall interests.

Briefs

  1. Interferometric Readout of Momentum-Space Topology in a Programmable Dissipative Photonic Circuit — Andrea Cataldo et al.
    A programmable photonic circuit interferometrically reads out momentum-space topology (Zak phase, Chern number) under non-Hermitian dissipative dynamics.
  2. Emergent Quantum Geometric Phases in Holey Graphene — Pablo Canteli et al.
    Patterned antidot lattices in monolayer graphene generate moiré-like commensurability and Brown-Zak oscillations without any twist or stacking, offering a clean synthetic platform for moire physics.
  3. Multi-Branch Transport in a Back-gated WS2 Transistor at Deep-Cryogenic Temperature — Megan Powell et al.
    Deep-cryogenic transport in a back-gated WS2 transistor shows unexplained multi-branch conduction features relevant to 2D TMD device physics.
  4. Weyl superconductivity from Feshbach resonance in the three-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model — Taekyoung Kim et al.
    Theoretical prediction of Weyl time-reversal-breaking superconductivity from a 3D Feshbach mechanism in the repulsive Hubbard model, a notable extension beyond the well-studied 2D case.
  5. Topological Transverse Transport without a Gap in Critical Topological Flat Bands — Chang-geun Oh et al.
    Develops finite-temperature Hall transport theory for critical topological flat bands that touch a continuum, showing quantization survives without a spectral gap—relevant to moire flat-band physics.
  6. Designing Strongly Correlated Quantum Phases of Matter with Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States — Alessandro Sinibaldi et al.
    Uses foundation neural-network quantum states for inverse design of Hamiltonians, identifying a new quantum spin liquid candidate via differentiable optimization over couplings.
  7. Theory of criticality-enabled U(1) symmetry breaking in a class of 1+1D systems — E. S. Andriyakhina et al.
    Analytic and DMRG theory of criticality-enabled spontaneous U(1) symmetry breaking at 1+1D Lifshitz points offers a surprising mechanism outside the usual Mermin-Wagner intuition.
  8. \muSR measurements of 3D Ising ferromagnetism in bulk Fe3GeTe2 crystals — M. N. Wilson et al.
    muSR measurements settle a long debate on Fe3GeTe2's low-temperature magnetic state, showing it's domain freezing rather than an AFM transition in this widely studied vdW ferromagnet.
  9. Anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping of thickness-quantized magnons — Tamara Azevedo et al.
    High-resolution spectroscopy reveals anisotropic, mode-dependent magnon damping in YIG films, refining standard magnonics assumptions.
  10. Many-body topology in parity-preserving tensor networks — Maksimilian Usoltcev et al.
    A minimal parity-preserving tensor network connects fermionic partition functions, loop gases, and toric-code physics, revealing a topological island with an exotic multicritical fixed point.

Quick mentions

  1. Surface quantum response of plasmonic heterodimers: revealing the hidden nonlocality — Ida Juliane Bundgaard et al.
    Quantum surface-response (Feibelman parameter) effects in plasmonic heterodimers can hide or reveal nonlocal corrections depending on probe type.
  2. Single-particle detection of the Néel transition in LaCrO3 microcrystals via widefield nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging — Carson O. Patterson et al.
    Widefield NV magnetometry resolves single-particle Néel transitions and domain pinning in LaCrO3 microcrystals.
  3. Giant PhotoMagnetoDiode Effect — V. L. Korenev et al.
    Observation of a giant photomagnetodiode rectification effect in GaAs under modest magnetic fields.
  4. Optical studies of negative g-factor dopants in an antiferromagnet: Nd:GdVO4 — Lachlan W. Cronin et al.
    Optical spectroscopy of Nd:GdVO4 below its Néel temperature reveals negative g-factor signatures useful for hybrid quantum systems.
  5. Reservoir- and Measurement-free Microwave Initialization of Semiconductor Spin Qubits — Leon C. Camenzind et al.
    Demonstrates fast reservoir- and measurement-free microwave initialization of silicon spin qubits with 99.4% fidelity.
  6. Fault Tolerant Quantum Phases of Matter — Colin V. Coane et al.
    Introduces a classification of fault-tolerant mixed-state quantum phases based on noise-robust local circuit equivalence.
  7. Sign problem and criticality in world-line quantum Monte Carlo methods — Rubem Mondaini et al.
    Shows that Kosterlitz-Thouless critical behavior of a reference boson model is imprinted on the average sign in world-line QMC simulations.
  8. Thermal magnon transport in FM/AFM bilayers — Moumita Kundu et al.
    Theoretical study finds thermally triggered chirality-selective spin currents in FM/AFM bilayers, relevant to magnonic device design.
  9. adapol: Adaptive pole-fitting for quantum many-body physics — Zhen Huang et al.
    Introduces adapol, a practical pole-fitting software package for Matsubara Green's functions used widely in quantum impurity solvers.
  10. Multipartite entanglement hidden in vector-chiral correlations of spin-1/2 chains — Tokuro Shimokawa
    Establishes a quantum Fisher information bound certifying multipartite entanglement from vector-chirality correlations in spin-1/2 chains, potentially measurable via dielectric spectroscopy.

item.title: Wed Sep 30: Dark interlayer excitons, layer-coherent polarons, and topology-forced exciton nodes
item.description:
Deep dives

  1. Interlayer dark excitons in a van der Waals heterostructure — Rundong Ma et al.
    Direct spectroscopic identification of bright vs dark interlayer excitons in dual-gated WSe2/hBN/WSe2 homobilayers, resolving a long-standing ambiguity central to interlayer exciton condensate physics.
  2. Interlayer Fermi Polarons in Bilayer MoTe2 — Ruihao Ni et al.
    Reveals a new layer-pseudospin Fermi polaron species in direct-gap bilayer MoTe2, extending polaron physics beyond monolayer TMDs with a clean optical platform relevant to your Fermi polaron interests.
  3. Topology Obstructs Nodeless Excitons — Lumen Eek
    Shows band topology can force nodal zeros in exciton envelope wavefunctions via the topology of the valence-conduction transition bundle, a conceptually new constraint on exciton physics verified with Bethe-Salpeter calculations.
  4. Interlayer coupling between twisted graphenes through atomically-precise barriers — Yueyang Wang et al.
    Demonstrates atomic-scale control of interlayer coupling in twisted bilayer graphene using hBN spacers, showing moiré hybridization survives surprisingly thick barriers—directly relevant to engineering moiré/vdW heterostructures.
  5. Spectroscopy of phonon-coupled integer and fractional Chern insulators: emergence of polarons and chirality deficit of graviton mode — Min Long et al.
    DMRG study reveals phonons dress excitons and magnetorotons into polaron-like composite modes in Chern/fractional Chern insulators, offering a unified excitation-based probe of FCI instabilities relevant to your moiré/QH interests.

Briefs

  1. Spin separation of Dirac electrons by twisted and vector optical beams — A. A. Gunyaga et al.
    Predicts that twisted and vector optical beams can spatially separate spin populations in TMD monolayers via structured-light-induced spin currents.
  2. Magnetoplasmon molecule — A. V. Larionov (Institute of Solid State Physics named after Yu. A. Osipyan et al.
    Reports a novel four-particle 'magnetoplasmon molecule' collective excitation in a 2D electron gas in high magnetic field, interacting with magnetoexciton condensates.
  3. Excitonic Stripe Order in the Two-Orbital Hubbard-Kanamori Model — Rafael D. Soares et al.
    Hartree-Fock study finds excitonic analogues of stripe order and spiral density waves in a two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model, connecting excitonic condensation to correlated stripe physics.
  4. Spatially dispersive photogalvanic effects as a probe of quantum geometric tensor — Yicong Chen et al.
    Uses spatially-dispersive photogalvanic effects in MoTe2 to cleanly separate quantum metric and Berry curvature contributions to photocurrents across a topological phase transition.
  5. Topological Band Theory for High-Dimensional Parameter Spaces — Vivek Chakrabhavi et al.
    Extends topological band theory of quantum Hall systems to high-dimensional parameter spaces, with an explicit hyperbolic band theory example relevant to synthetic-dimension QH platforms.
  6. Artificial versus Natural Atoms: The uncanny capability of the many-body Schrödinger equation to produce emergent behavior — Constantine Yannouleas
    Review of Wigner molecule physics in artificial atoms including moiré TMD quantum dots, offering an alternative theoretical lens on fractional quantum Hall-adjacent correlated states.
  7. Nonlinear optical responses of semiconducting graphene nanoribbons: Strong constraint from a hidden symmetry — Jiawei Ruan et al.
    Identifies a hidden bipartite particle-hole symmetry that suppresses even-order nonlinear optical responses in graphene nanoribbons, enabling pure spin photocurrents tunable by magnetic field.
  8. Neural-quantum-state based downfolding of the three-band Emery model for cuprates and nickelates — Hannah Lange et al.
    Neural quantum states scale downfolding of the three-band Emery model to 300 sites, revealing that effective single-band cuprate/nickelate models require significant beyond-Hubbard terms.
  9. Deep Learning GW Quasiparticle Hamiltonians for Many-Body Excited-State Electronic Structure at Scale — Xiaoxun Gong et al.
    A deep-learning framework predicts GW quasiparticle Hamiltonians directly from atomic structure with meV accuracy and strong transferability to larger supercells, a potential game-changer for excited-state calculations relevant to 2D materials.
  10. Multistate Torsion in Zitterbewegung — Wojciech J. Jankowski
    Derives nonlinear Zitterbewegung velocity augmented by quantum geometric torsion, predicting transient photocurrent signatures distinct from known circularly-polarized-light photovoltaic effects.

Quick mentions

  1. 3/8 charge-density wave instability in the kagome metal CsV3Sb5 — Luca Buiarelli et al.
    DFPT calculations explain a pressure-induced 3/8 charge-density-wave instability in kagome metal CsV3Sb5 coinciding with its superconducting dome dip.
  2. Reversible field-free superconducting diode effect controlled by an antiferromagnet — Filip Krizek et al.
    Demonstrates a field-free superconducting diode effect controlled by a collinear antiferromagnet without spin splitting or net magnetization.
  3. Unveiling Three-Dimensional Skyrmion Transitions Through Vortices and Monopoles — Melissa E. Henderson et al.
    First experimental neutron-tomography visualization of 3D topological Q=0 skyrmion structures and meron-monopole mediated transitions in a bulk chiral magnet.
  4. Advancing Fuzzy-Sphere CFTs: SO(3)-Rotation-Resolving Exact Diagonalization, 3D Ising Heavy Primaries, and Quasi-Hole-Space Projection — Zheng Zhou et al.
    Major advance in fuzzy-sphere regularization of 3D CFTs identifies ~100 primary operators in the 3D Ising CFT and links critical points to fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions.
  5. Uniform-Charge-Density d-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure t-J Model at 1/8 Doping on an Infinite Cylinder — Guangyu Yu et al.
    VUMPS calculations on infinite cylinders find uniform-charge-density d-wave superconductivity rather than stripe order in the pure t-J model at 1/8 doping, addressing a long-standing numerical controversy.
  6. Frustrated Gd3+ Double Perovskites as High-Performance Magnetocaloric Materials for Sub-100 mK Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration — Tim Treu et al.
    Gd3+ double perovskites achieve record sub-100 mK adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration temperatures, promising for cooling quantum technology platforms.
  7. Ohm's law for information revealed by a skyrmion Maxwell's demon — Soma Miki et al.
    Realizes an 'Ohm's law for information' using a room-temperature skyrmion-based Maxwell's demon information engine.
  8. Imaging phase winding in topological superconductors with a fork-tip Josephson STM — Vladislav Poliakov et al.
    Proposes a fork-tip Josephson STM interferometer scheme to directly image phase winding in topological superconductors.
  9. Correlation-assisted topological and metamagnetic transitions in Rashba-coupled superconductors: t-J-U model study — Tushar Dey et al.
    Finds a correlation-driven Chern number C=±2 topological superconducting state in a Rashba-coupled t-J-U model, distinct from weak-coupling BdG results.
  10. Probing the electronic structure of UTe2 with ARPES and high-energy spectroscopy — Shin-ichi Fujimori
    Review synthesizing ARPES and X-ray spectroscopy evidence for an intermediate-valence 5f2/5f3 ground state in the unconventional superconductor UTe2.

  5. Uniform-Charge-Density d-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure t-J Model at 1/8 Doping on an Infinite Cylinder — Guangyu Yu et al.
    VUMPS calculations on infinite cylinders find uniform-charge-density d-wave superconductivity rather than stripe order in the pure t-J model at 1/8 doping, addressing a long-standing numerical controversy.
  6. Frustrated Gd3+ Double Perovskites as High-Performance Magnetocaloric Materials for Sub-100 mK Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration — Tim Treu et al.
    Gd3+ double perovskites achieve record sub-100 mK adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration temperatures, promising for cooling quantum technology platforms.
  7. Ohm's law for information revealed by a skyrmion Maxwell's demon — Soma Miki et al.
    Realizes an 'Ohm's law for information' using a room-temperature skyrmion-based Maxwell's demon information engine.
  8. Imaging phase winding in topological superconductors with a fork-tip Josephson STM — Vladislav Poliakov et al.
    Proposes a fork-tip Josephson STM interferometer scheme to directly image phase winding in topological superconductors.
  9. Correlation-assisted topological and metamagnetic transitions in Rashba-coupled superconductors: t-J-U model study — Tushar Dey et al.
    Finds a correlation-driven Chern number C=±2 topological superconducting state in a Rashba-coupled t-J-U model, distinct from weak-coupling BdG results.
  10. Probing the electronic structure of UTe2 with ARPES and high-energy spectroscopy — Shin-ichi Fujimori
    Review synthesizing ARPES and X-ray spectroscopy evidence for an intermediate-valence 5f2/5f3 ground state in the unconventional superconductor UTe2.
